title: a restore that said its interrupt ends 130, whatever signal comes next
note: basis 'shown' means shown in train 176's job log (job 138877998556) and by the card's unit tests on master 6c73db64 and on the branch; the rehearsal itself runs only in CI and was not run here.

findings.claim: trialbox restore said its interrupt and returned 130, then its finally put the default SIGTERM handler back; the walk's second SIGTERM before the exit killed it (143, train 176 step 28); the installed command now ignores further signals on its own way out after a said 130, in-process callers keep their handlers

between _restore's stop_signals() and the __main__ block's _exit_code (the lock's release and the returns) a second signal still gets the default action; closing it needs _restore to know it runs as the process
